provenance.source: Gelir Vergisi Kanunu md. 103 ve gecici 91; 5510 sayili Kanun (SGK); PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Turkey; Alomaliye and TURMOB 2026 payroll parameters
provenance.notes: The five 2026 employment income bands came from PwC. The SGK employee rate of 14%, unemployment 1%, the monthly ceiling of TRY 297,270 and the gross minimum wage of TRY 33,030 came from Turkish payroll summaries read on 31 August 2026.

verificationTodo: Confirm the minimum wage exemption mechanism, which exempts the income tax attributable to the minimum wage. This app applies it as an annual credit rather than month by month.
Confirm the SGK monthly ceiling of TRY 297,270, which is nine times the gross minimum wage.
The stamp duty exemption on the minimum wage is not modelled.
omissions: Stamp duty on wages, currently 0.759%, is not modelled.

Turkish withholding is cumulative through the year, so the month in which you cross a bracket changes your net pay. This app computes the annual liability rather than reproducing the monthly cumulative withholding.
The disability allowance and private pension deductions are not modelled.

brackets.legalRef: GVK md. 103, employment income scale for 2026
brackets.note: Turkey applies a separate, more generous scale to employment income than to other income.

sgk.note: The employee pays 14% social security plus 1% unemployment insurance, both on pay up to a monthly ceiling of nine times the gross minimum wage.

minimumWageExemption.note: The income tax attributable to the minimum wage is exempt for every employee, not only for those earning it. In practice it works as a credit equal to the tax that would be due on a minimum-wage salary.

regions.name: Turkiye
regions.note: Turkish income tax has no regional component.

inputSchema.label: Brut ucret (per month)
inputSchema.help: Gross monthly pay. SGK is capped monthly, so a bonus month does not raise your contributions beyond the ceiling.

inputSchema.label: Kesilen gelir vergisi (per month)
inputSchema.help: Income tax withheld each month, for the annual comparison. Turkish withholding is cumulative, so it rises through the year.
